overall: Thursday, June 25 should bring a warm and mostly sunny day to Washington, DC, with temperatures climbing into the upper 80s to near 90°F. South winds of 7–10 mph with gusts up to 23 mph will support warming, and no precipitation is expected. This is the last fully dry day before a pattern shift brings a 50% chance of thunderstorms Friday afternoon and increasing rain through the weekend.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is reasonably strong, with ECMWF (87.5°F), NBM (88.5°F), HRRR (89.5°F), and WEATHER_COM (87.1°F) all clustering in the 87–90°F range. The GFS is a clear outlier at 77.6°F expected TMAX — well below the consensus and inconsistent with the prior-day observed high of 84.2°F — suggesting the GFS should be down-weighted; the full ensemble expected TMAX of 87.6°F reflects this adjustment.
max_temp_prediction: The active even-bucket market shows the 90–91°F bucket as the strong modal leader at 49.7% probability (Tier 1 high confidence, 21-point gap over the 2nd bucket at 84–85F), though the full ensemble expected TMAX of 87.6°F and NWS forecast of 'near 88°F' suggest the central tendency sits just below the top bucket. The mostly sunny sky, southerly flow, and warm antecedent conditions (prior-day high 84.2°F) support a meaningful warm push, pointing to a high in the 88–90°F range; the 90–91°F bucket remains the single most likely outcome but the bulk of probability mass (including 88–89F at ~19.6%) straddles the 88–91°F zone.
